title: App Not Detected After Install (0x87D1041C)
description: Detects when Intune's detection check right after an app's installer finished did not find the app, so Intune reports the install as failed (0x87D1041C).
explanation:
The Intune Management Extension runs an app's detection twice: before the install, to decide whether the install is needed, and right after the installer finishes. Here the installer finished, but the check afterwards did not find the app. Intune therefore reports the install as failed with **0x87D1041C** (*application not detected after installation completed successfully*), even though the installer itself succeeded.

For Win32 apps the detection rule does not match what the installer left on the device. Common causes:

- The rule checks a path or registry key the installer does not create (wrong path, version folder or bitness, e.g. HKLM\SOFTWARE\... versus HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\...).
- The installer finishes its work later (an async task, a service, or a restart it needs but does not request with a restart return code), after the check has run.
- A detection script exits 0 without writing to stdout, which Intune treats as not detected.
- The installer writes to the user profile while the rule looks in system scope, or the other way round.

Microsoft Store (WinGet) apps have no detection rule to edit: Intune asks WinGet whether the package is installed in the app's install context.

When the installer requests a restart with its return code, Intune checks again after the restart; this finding then means the app was still missing afterwards.

remediation.title: Check the detection rule against an installed device
steps: Open the app in Intune → Properties → Detection rules and note exactly what the rule checks
Install the app on a test device outside Autopilot and confirm that the file, registry key or script result exists right after the installer exits
For registry rules, check both HKLM\SOFTWARE\... and HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\... depending on the installer's bitness
For script rules, run the script as SYSTEM: it must write at least one line to stdout and exit 0 when the app is present
If the installer completes its work later, detect something it writes synchronously, such as the MSI product code under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\

remediation.title: Microsoft Store (WinGet) apps
steps: Check the package identifier and the install behavior (System or User) of the app in Intune
Install the package manually in the same context on a test device and confirm it is reported as installed
